guard: the source orders a session by the id PAIR, stops at the first part that is not settled, settles a part its turn has ended, never lets a user part gate the stream, and reports a vanished cursor once
why: EVERY CELL NAMED HERE WAS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE MUTATION RAN, not chosen afterwards from
whatever went red. The four properties below are the ones the design turns on, and three of them
were reached by measuring a real store rather than by reading the plan:
1. AUTHORSHIP GATES BEFORE PART TYPE. A user message carries no completion mark, the field does
not exist on its type, and 659 of 668 user text parts carry no clock at all, so under a
type-first rule neither settle signal can ever arrive and the stream wedges at the first
prompt of every session. This is the defect the suite exists to keep dead.
2. THE READ STOPS AT THE FIRST UNSETTLED PART. 1657 of 11298 parts that have a successor are
updated AFTER that successor exists, so emitting around one would publish out of bracket order
and advancing past it would drop it for good.
3. THE CURSOR IS THE PAIR. Part ids invert across a message boundary 16 times in 14759 ordered
pairs, so a bare part-id comparison silently skips.
4. A VANISHED CURSOR IS REPORTED ONCE. A revert leaves it absent on every later read, so a
per-read report would bury the next, different divergence in its own noise.
BLAST RADIUS IS STATED PER MUTATION rather than discovered by a later reader. A mutant that reds
more than the cell expectRed names is neither a clean kill nor a failure, and the count belongs
EVERY ANCHOR IS PURE CODE. None spans a comment, so rewording the prose around one cannot turn a
mutant into a no-op that reports the same green a holding guard reports.

mutations.name: S3 the cursor compares the part id alone, dropping the message half of the pair
mutations.expectRed: cursor:resuming after the first message yields the LOWER-id part in the next message

mutations.name: S4 the turn-level backstop is removed, so a part whose turn ended without per-part marks never settles
